title: I Am Come Into My Garden
summary: After the long seeking through doctrine, the soul passes through and finds what it has been seeking — and finds it in the inmost. What is given here is exactly that inmost: what Greatness is, and why the title Father belongs to the Lord wherever he stands as source; the First Father in his fivefold articulation, with the procession of light, fragrance, voice, greatness, and revelation that issues from him; the Land of Light, the inmost country where everything lives by him alone, with no mingling, no falsity, no death; and the eternity of what is given, which stands from before any beginning the soul can name, set against what is claimed by the self, whose end is fixed within itself. The brevity is accuracy: the inmost cannot be elaborated; it can only be entered. The section is short because the conjunction itself is — and the next state will undo this first reception so that a deeper one may be made.
organizing_principle: The four teachings move from the threshold inward. The first names the door: Greatness as the bearing-realm, Father as the title given wherever the Lord stands as foundation. The second enters: the First Father in his five members and twelve registers, the inmost articulated unity. The third looks around at what is in this country: the Land of Light, where there is no mingling, no falsity, no death — the soul received as gift recognizes itself for what it is. The fourth names the temporal character of what is found: eternity, that which stands from before eternity, set against the bounded ending of what is claimed by the self. This is the first conjunction in the cycle. It is brief because brevity is the truth of it: what the soul has just touched is precisely what cannot be possessed. The role here is a local culmination — a real peak that opens into the next section's deeper work — not the book's ultimate consummation, which belongs to the close.
